paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the loss values over a range of iteration numbers for different models. The x-axis represents the iteration number, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, and tick labels spaced at regular intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, with a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, and tick labels spaced at regular intervals of 0.1. The plot contains six lines, each representing a different model: Vanilla (purple, solid), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid), and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue, solid). Starting at approximately 3.3, the Vanilla line decreases steeply to around 2.65 at 20,000 iterations, then gradually declines to about 2.55 at 140,000 iterations. The StrmLLM (n=64) line begins at 3.25, drops sharply to 2.7 at 20,000 iterations, and then steadily decreases to 2.6 at 140,000 iterations. The SepLLM lines start between 3.25 and 3.2, decline rapidly to 2.65-2.7 at 20,000 iterations, and then gradually decrease to 2.55-2.6 at 140,000 iterations. Each line exhibits a similar trend of rapid initial decline followed by a steady decrease.
